newsitem.title: UK: Continental axes ex-UK, Germany surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Continental axes ex-UK, Germany surcharges.

text.p: U.S. carrier Continental Airlines said it dropped its ex-UK and ex-Germany cargo fuel surcharges applicable to tranatlantic routes from April 12.

UK cargo manager Brian Coleman told Reuters that he had asked for, and received, head office permission to drop the surcharge implemented last November as he felt fuel prices had since dropped to a more acceptable level.
They were the equivalent of 10 U.S. cents per kg, or six pence per kg in the UK.
"Apart from the UK and Germany, I cannot comment on the decisions of the other Continental European stations -- in Madrid and Paris -- regarding the surcharge," he said.
But Coleman added that Continental was retaining its ex-U.S. transatlantic cargo fuel surcharge.
On April 15, the carrier's cargo marketing manager Dana Bates told Reuters her airline's fuel costs had not come down sufficiently and it would retain the ex-U.S. surcharge indefinitely.
